things._comment: THE SPEND GATE. read wallet config rows (find-current-items) + open reservation (idempotency) -> decide() pure script -> write budget_check + budget_reservation (per-operation address AND the fixed default-work-control mirror the AgentWalletPanel reads). Input: operation_ref, estimated_cost (USD cents), spender_id (agent_id compatibility accepted), idempotency_key. Output: {approved, reason, check_ref, reservation_ref}. The CALLER inspects approved: false -> stop + emit AgentBlockedInsufficientBudget; true -> proceed carrying reservation_ref. A pending_setup/disabled authority DENIES every positive-cost request; a validated zero-cost request receives a zero-amount fence without consuming wallet authority.

payload.name: budget-gate
payload.description: Structural pre-operation spend gate: read the selected spend-authority DATA, decide approve/deny against status+enabled+daily_limit+auto_approve_threshold, and write a spend_budget_check + spend_budget_reservation the caller must carry forward or block on. Rail-agnostic, status-string-opaque, fail-closed.

estimated_cost.description: Positive integer minor units; zero-cost work still gets an auditable reservation.

spend_authority_ref.description: Live-log service connection holding this rail's status, limits, and totals.

steps._comment: Wallet config is read PER-PROPERTY via engine.operation.read-current. Live-log facts (write-batch) are readable this way at their identity address; they are NOT in the find-current-items projection (that index is populated by package admission, not write-batch — proven: read-current finds the selected rail facts, find-current-items returns []). Each read returns output.payload.value_json (a JSON-encoded scalar). Absent -> the decide script applies fail-closed defaults.

IDEMPOTENCY read: the existing per-operation reservation. Read at DEFAULT mode (no address_mode) because the write step persists this address hashed (runtime write ignores address_mode; non-'|' addresses are hashed — stores/mod.rs), so the read MUST match (default/hash). Absent on first call -> the decide script treats it as no prior reservation. The address is the same concat the write uses.

Only a process has a wall clock — workflow bindings have no 'now'. This tiny process prints the current ISO time on stdout so the decide step and the check expiry are anchored to real time, not a binding.

argv._comment: argv[3] = wallet status value_json (read-current payload.value_json). Absent -> '' -> fail-closed default pending_setup.
argv[4] = wallet enabled value_json. Absent -> '' -> fail-closed false.

argv[8] = the action input payload (operation_ref, estimated_cost, spend_authority_ref, rail_ref, spender_id, compatibility aliases, idempotency_key, ttl_seconds). The script is rail-agnostic and fails closed on absent authority DATA.
argv[9] = the wall-clock now from the now step (workflow bindings have no clock). The script anchors check + reservation expiry to this.

argv[10] = the existing per-op reservation (IDEMPOTENCY). A still-current reservation for the same idempotency_key short-circuits to an idempotent approval — no re-approve, no double-count. Absent -> {} -> treated as no prior reservation.

steps._comment: Write the budget_check + budget_reservation. FOUR writes: (1) per-operation budget_check at package::agent-wallet::budget-check::<op_slug> (audit trail, never clobbered by concurrent ops), (2) the fixed default-work-control budget-check mirror the AgentWalletPanel reads (it can't discover per-op addresses), (3) per-operation budget_reservation, (4) the fixed default-work-control reservation mirror. ADDRESS MODE: runtime write IGNORES address_mode (step_executor build_writes never reads it) — a non-'|' address is ALWAYS hashed (stores/mod.rs runtime_fact_address), matching the existing seed default-work-control records the panel reads via label_hash. So these per-op + mirror addresses are hash-addressed; readers use label_hash. The reservation is ALWAYS a real object (status current on approval, denied on denial) — NEVER null — so every write has a concrete payload (payload:null = retract, types.rs PendingWrite). SSOT: check is the decision record; reservation is the double-spend fence. The caller proceeds/blocks on budget_check.result, NOT on reservation presence.

extra.gate_boundary: structural pre-operation spend authorization; fail-closed on malformed or positive-cost requests against a non-active/disabled/over-limit wallet; zero-cost requests receive a zero-amount fence
extra.side_effect_boundary: writes budget_check + budget_reservation records ONLY; never performs the payment

things._comment: DAILY SPEND RESET — pure DATA. On the clock tick, a python gate decides whether the UTC day has rolled over since the last reset marker; if so, write total_spent_today = 0 (both the identity_text attribute_fact the engine assembles AND the value the gate reads) + advance the reset marker. Single-flight via the marker (mirrors agents-hub spawn-decision single-flight): overlapping ticks within the same UTC day are no-ops. Decision != side-effect: the reset write is gated on the python EXIT CODE (0 == roll-over), so a same-day tick Skips the write cleanly.
things.name: decide-daily-reset-mjs

payload.name: reset-daily-spend
payload.description: Clock-triggered rail-agnostic daily spend reset: if the UTC day rolled over since the selected authority's reset marker, zero its total_spent_today and advance the marker. Single-flight; pure DATA; never touches money.

steps._comment: Read the last-reset marker at DEFAULT mode (the write persists default mode; the read must match for single-flight to see the prior reset). Absent on first run -> gate treats as never-reset and resets once.

Pure roll-over decision. argv: <last_reset_marker_json>. Only a process has a wall clock. Outputs {should_reset, now_iso, day} on stdout; exit code 0 == should_reset (the gating edges read exit_code, the marker write reads now_iso). exit 3 == same day (no-op).

Zero total_spent_today (identity_text attribute_fact the engine assembles) + advance the reset marker (default mode). Gated by the on_result edge gate->write_reset (exit_code == 0). value_json is the STRING "0" (attribute_fact values are JSON-encoded scalars; integer 0 encodes as "0").

edges._comment: Gate on the EXIT CODE (0 == day rolled over), NOT stdout: a compute.process step's stdout is a byte side-channel the EDGE resolver cannot materialize; exit_code IS inline. exit 3 (same day) -> condition false -> write Skipped (no-op tick).

things._comment: SPEND-LEDGER INCREMENT — pure DATA. Runs AFTER a payment actually succeeds (called by action:apply-x402-payment, #102b). read wallet totals + now -> record-spend.mjs adds the amount (the engine has no arithmetic binding op) -> write total_spent_today + total_spent_all_time (identity_text attribute_facts the engine assembles) + a payment_processed audit record. Records reality; never authorizes. This is the post-payment counterpart to the pre-payment budget-gate.
things.name: record-spend-mjs

payload.name: record-spend
payload.description: Post-payment rail-agnostic spend-ledger increment: add a confirmed spend amount to the selected authority's total_spent_today + total_spent_all_time and write a spend_payment_processed audit record. Pure DATA; records reality, never authorizes.

steps._comment: Prior totals read PER-PROPERTY via read-current (live-log facts are read by address, NOT find-current-items). Absent -> the script defaults to 0.

argv._comment: argv[5] = spend payload (amount, operation_ref, spend_authority_ref, rail_ref, spender_id, payment evidence).

steps._comment: Write the new spend totals (identity_text attribute_facts the engine assembles, value_json = JSON-encoded integer string) + a payment_processed audit record at package::agent-wallet::payment::<op_slug>. The totals come from the ledger script's computed sums (current + amount), NOT a stale binding.

things._comment: DAILY-RESET CADENCE TRIGGER — EXACT clone of the proven agents-hub trigger:spawn-decision-on-clock-tick shape, dispatching to action:reset-daily-spend. is_active:FALSE — the team-lead flips it true after review (zero runaway risk during build). The single-flight UTC-day gate inside the def is the real safety; this flag is the second gate. Topic clock-tick, delta, match clock::tick.
